extracted.intended_audience: individual fellowship applicants (students and early-career researchers) who received a rejection
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, step-by-step advice for applicants whose fellowship applications were rejected: understand why, seek feedback, reflect on materials and interview, build skills and networks, explore alternative funding, and plan for reapplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand reasons behind the rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The first step in moving forward is to understand the reasons behind the rejection. Rejection does not necessarily reflect your worth or potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common reasons include a lack of alignment between your goals and the program’s objectives, insufficient experience in the field, or a highly competitive applicant pool. By identifying these factors you can gain insights to strengthen future applications and develop a more targeted approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek feedback from the selection committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Request insights from the selection committee about their decision-making and specific areas for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach the committee with professionalism and gratitude—send a well-crafted email expressing appreciation and politely asking for specific areas to improve. Many committees are open to providing constructive responses that can guide revisions to your personal statement, experience-building, or project focus. Engaging this way demonstrates commitment to growth and helps build rapport for future applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach feedback requests with professionalism and gratitude
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting feedback, be professional and grateful to maximize the chance of receiving useful guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A polite, appreciative request that asks for specific areas of improvement can yield constructive responses. This helps you understand the committee’s perspective and expectations and signals willingness to learn—potentially benefiting future applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect on your application and interview performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct an introspective evaluation of submitted materials and interview performance to identify inconsistencies, gaps, or unclear elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review whether you clearly articulated goals and motivations, check for narrative inconsistencies, and consider how well you communicated ideas and passion in interviews. Use mock interviews and mentor guidance to refine interview skills and prepare stronger future submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider seeking additional training or experience
rubrics_metrics.description: If reflection reveals gaps in qualifications or experience, pursue training or opportunities to bolster your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include enrolling in relevant courses, attending workshops, pursuing internships, volunteering, or engaging in community projects related to your field. New skills and practical experience both strengthen your resume and demonstrate commitment to continuous learning while providing networking opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore other funding opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Broaden your search beyond the single fellowship to discover other grants, scholarships, fellowships, or alternative funding sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research a variety of opportunities—traditional funders, crowdfunding platforms, community-based initiatives, local organizations, and academic institutions—to find better alignment with your goals and increase chances of securing support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network with current and former fellows
rubrics_metrics.description: Connect with past and current fellows to gain firsthand insights into their experiences and the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend networking events, join online forums, or participate in social media groups related to the fellowship. Peers can share tips, pitfalls, and mentorship opportunities that help you tailor your application more effectively and expand professional connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay positive and persistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a constructive mindset after rejection; resilience and persistence improve long-term success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember many successful people faced rejection; surround yourself with supportive mentors and peers, set specific goals (skills to gain, experiences to pursue), celebrate small victories, and use rejection as motivation to improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapply in the future after improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider reapplying once you have acted on feedback, gained new skills, and addressed weaknesses in your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many applicants succeed on their second or third attempts—when reapplying, highlight new experiences and explicitly address feedback received to demonstrate growth and a clear strategy for improvement.
